title: Vic's 2024 essay: Affistash MRR up 442%, a SaaS exit, and the cost of hustle at 18
summary: Vic's personal year-in-review as an 18-year-old software founder. He recounts growing Affistash with an audience co-founder, the marketing channels that moved revenue, a quick SaaS exit via Twitter, and the anxiety and relationship lessons behind the business growth.

principles.text: Find an audience co-founder: putting in real marketing work on the product is what made revenue grow.
principles.quote: My co-founder and i started putting in the work on marketing Affistash and the revenue started growing which gave me a ton of motivation to keep building software

principles.text: Sell small products by tweeting: a semi-viral post produced 10-15 interested buyers and a quick exit.
principles.quote: Posted a tweet (went semi-viral) * Got 10-15 DMs of interested people looking to buy * Sold to a big CTO from California

principles.text: Stack many channels: pSEO, cold email, content, conferences, landing page and onboarding improvements together drove growth.
principles.quote: pSEO (I created a python script and Framer CMS to index 5000 pages)

principles.text: Cold email worked well with a small setup of 6 mailboxes, with reply rates around 15%.
principles.quote: Cold email (purchased 6 mailboxes and we got around 15% reply rate which was insane - still working on automating the reply process)

principles.text: Moving the landing page from NextJS to Framer lifted conversion; track where users come from during onboarding.
principles.quote: Updated the landing page (moved from NextJS to Framer and the conversion rates improved a lot)

principles.text: Relationships matter more than money; losing people hurts far more than churn or disputes.
principles.quote: losing relationships with people that you care about is 1000x more painful than any customer dispute, any churn or any lost money
